To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the authors demonstrate miniaturized gated field emitter arrays by different molding techniques.

1) High tip density gated field emitters arrays (FEDAs) with submicron emitter base sizes and submicron emitter pitch can be realized by using molding technique, 2) the emitter size can be controlled by the mold size and the emitter pitch can be controlled by using different mask designs, 3) the emitter size is determined by the size of the mold, the emitter pitch is determined by the mask design.
we have demonstrated a new method to fabricate gated all-metal field emitter with a submicron emitter pitch and 200nm emitter base size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of gated all-metal field emitter array structures with high tip density, high emission current density and small emission area.
the fabrication and characterization of high tip density gated field emitters arrays with submicrometer emitter pitch.
the fabrication of gated all-metal field emitter array (FEA) cathodes with submicron emitter pitch and 200 nanometers (nm) emitter base size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that it is feasible to fabricate gated all-metal field emitter array with submicron emitter pitch, and that the emitter base size can be further reduced.
the field emission performance is strongly influenced by the geometry of the emitter tip, the emitter base, and the gate structure.
a combination of the two approaches, i.e., the molding technique and the tip sharpening process, is most promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated a novel approach for fabricating high-density, low-threshold voltage, high current density field emitter arrays by molding technique, which is suitable for high resolution flat panel display applications.
we are the first to report the fabrication of all-metal FEAs with a submicron emitter pitch and 200nm emitter base size.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the molding technique for the fabrication of high tip density gated field emitters arrays (FEMs).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emitter size can be reduced by 1 order of magnitude by using a molding technique.
the gate electrode and emitter tip are not required to be fabricated at the same time.
the emitter tip density can be increased to 1 million tips/mm2.
